State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure that creates a new asset or improves an existing asset beyond its original standard is capital expenditure.

options.A: True - because Capital expenditure results in the acquisition of new assets or the enhancement of existing ones.
options.B: False - because Any expenditure sanctioned by the Railway Board is capital expenditure.
options.C: True - because Expenditure on existing assets can never be capital expenditure.
options.D: False - because All expenditure on railway property is capital expenditure by default.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
All expenditure incurred on existing railway assets is revenue expenditure.

options.A: True - because Asset renewals are working expenses under Demand 4.
options.B: False - because Renewals and replacements of assets are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, not to revenue.
options.C: True - because Revenue covers every kind of expenditure on existing assets.
options.D: False - because The DRF is only a notional reserve with no real expenditure.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Day-to-day repairs that keep an asset in good working condition are revenue expenditure.

options.A: True - because Repairs are capitalised whenever they exceed one lakh rupees.
options.B: False - because All repair expenditure is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
options.C: True - because Revenue expenditure maintains assets in working order without adding to their value.
options.D: False - because Repairs that prevent accidents are always capital expenditure.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure on surveys for new lines is always charged to capital.

options.A: True - because Surveys are never charged to revenue under any circumstance.
options.B: False - because All surveys are charged to the Development Fund.
options.C: True - because Survey expenditure is written off to suspense permanently.
options.D: False - because Surveys are charged to revenue unless the work is sanctioned, in which case they go to capital.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The cost of constructing a new railway line is capital expenditure.

options.A: True - because A new line creates a new asset and is charged to Capital under Demand 16.
options.B: False - because New lines are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
options.C: True - because New lines are charged to revenue because they earn traffic receipts.
options.D: False - because New line construction is met from the Staff Benefit Fund.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Maintenance of railway bridges is capital expenditure.

options.A: True - because Bridge repairs are met from the Capital Fund.
options.B: False - because Bridge maintenance is revenue expenditure under Abstract B.
options.C: True - because Bridge maintenance creates new assets and is capitalised.
options.D: False - because All bridge expenditure is charged to Plan Head 32.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure on replacement of rails and sleepers is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

options.A: True - because Rail replacements are met from the Capital Fund.
options.B: False - because Track renewals are charged to revenue as working expenses.
options.C: True - because Renewals and replacements of assets are financed from the DRF.
options.D: False - because Renewals are charged to the Development Fund.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Capital expenditure of the railways does not require Parliament's approval.

options.A: True - because Parliament has no role in capital budgeting.
options.B: False - because Capital expenditure is sanctioned by the Railway Board alone.
options.C: True - because Capital works are approved by the General Manager.
options.D: False - because Capital works under Demand 16 are voted by Parliament.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Stores consumed in routine maintenance are charged to revenue.

options.A: True - because Consumption of stores for maintenance is ordinary working expenditure.
options.B: False - because Consumed stores remain charged to Stores Suspense permanently.
options.C: True - because Store consumption is capitalised as asset value.
options.D: False - because Consumed stores are debited to Miscellaneous Advances.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The cost of track renewal is met from revenue.

options.A: True - because Renewals are charged to Abstract B as maintenance.
options.B: False - because Track renewals are financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund.
options.C: True - because Track renewal is ordinary working expenditure.
options.D: False - because The DRF is not used for track renewals.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure on new rolling stock is charged to Capital under Plan Head 21.

options.A: True - because Rolling stock purchases are charged to the Pension Fund.
options.B: False - because New locomotives are met from the Development Fund.
options.C: True - because New rolling stock is an acquisition of assets under Demand 16.
options.D: False - because Rolling stock is charged to revenue under Abstract F.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Repairs arising from accidents are always charged to revenue.

options.A: True - because Accident repairs are charged to the Staff Benefit Fund.
options.B: False - because Accident renewals need no budget provision.
options.C: True - because Accident damage is always a revenue charge.
options.D: False - because Accident renewals are charged to the fund or head that bears the asset, normally the DRF.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Betterment of an asset beyond its original capacity is capital expenditure.

options.A: True - because Improvements that enhance an asset's utility beyond the original standard are capitalised.
options.B: False - because Betterment is always charged to revenue as maintenance.
options.C: True - because Betterment works are financed from the Staff Benefit Fund.
options.D: False - because Any improvement to an asset is revenue expenditure.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Depreciation is charged only in the year in which an asset is scrapped.

options.A: True - because Depreciation is a one-time charge at the end of asset life.
options.B: False - because Appropriation to the DRF is made every year to provide for future renewals.
options.C: True - because Depreciation is charged only for rolling stock.
options.D: False - because No annual provision for depreciation is made in railway accounts.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The cost of land acquired for railway purposes is capital expenditure.

options.A: True - because Land is charged to a suspense head until it is sold.
options.B: False - because Land cost is charged to revenue in the year of purchase.
options.C: True - because Land acquisition creates a permanent asset for the railway.
options.D: False - because Land acquisition is met from the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Open line works chargeable to revenue are debited to capital.

options.A: True - because Revenue works are charged to the Capital Fund.
options.B: False - because OLWR is debited to Plan Head 64.
options.C: True - because All open line works are capital works.
options.D: False - because Open line works revenue (OLWR) is charged to revenue, not to capital.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Interest paid on capital during the construction of a work is capitalised.

options.A: True - because Interest during construction forms part of the cost of the asset created.
options.B: False - because Interest on capital is never recognised in railway accounts.
options.C: True - because Interest during construction is charged to revenue as finance cost.
options.D: False - because Interest is written off to the Development Fund.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Railway Board can reappropriate provision from one grant to another.

options.A: True - because Inter-grant transfers are within the Board's powers.
options.B: False - because Reappropriation between grants is not permissible; a supplementary grant is needed.
options.C: True - because Grants are fully fungible after the budget is passed.
options.D: False - because The Board needs only Finance Ministry concurrence for inter-grant transfers.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Compensation paid to staff for loss of property is revenue expenditure.

options.A: True - because All compensation is charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund.
options.B: False - because Staff compensation is charged to the Capital Fund.
options.C: True - because Staff compensation is a working expense booked under the relevant demand.
options.D: False - because Compensation is debited to the Pension Fund.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
A General Manager can reappropriate provision between any two demands.

options.A: True - because The General Manager's powers extend across all demands.
options.B: False - because Demands are only indicative and fully interchangeable.
options.C: True - because Inter-demand reappropriation needs no authority.
options.D: False - because Reappropriation is permitted only within a grant, between its sub-heads.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation of provision from one grant to another is not permissible.

options.A: True - because Each grant is voted separately by Parliament, so inter-grant transfers need fresh Parliamentary approval.
options.B: False - because Inter-grant reappropriation needs only the General Manager's approval.
options.C: True - because Grants are interchangeable once the budget is passed.
options.D: False - because The Railway Board may freely move funds between any two grants.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Savings under a charged appropriation can be used to meet voted expenditure.

options.A: True - because Charged savings are available for voted use with Board approval.
options.B: False - because No reappropriation is permitted between charged and voted heads.
options.C: True - because The distinction between charged and voted is only nominal.
options.D: False - because Charged heads lapse into voted heads at year end.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
No reappropriation is permitted from a Charged head to a Voted head or vice versa.

options.A: True - because The President's sanction covers charged and voted heads together.
options.B: False - because Voted and Charged heads are interchangeable within a demand.
options.C: True - because Charged and Voted provisions are distinct appropriations carrying different sanctions.
options.D: False - because Charged savings may be used for voted expenditure with Board approval.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation can be sanctioned after the close of the financial year.

options.A: True - because The Board permits reappropriation in April for the previous year.
options.B: False - because Year-end reappropriation is routine practice.
options.C: True - because Reappropriation is allowed until the accounts are finalised.
options.D: False - because No reappropriation is permissible after the 31st of March.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Under Demand 16, no reappropriation is permitted between Capital, Railway Funds and Revenue.

options.A: True - because These are separate segments of the works grant and funds cannot be moved between them.
options.B: False - because The Board may move funds between Capital and Revenue under Demand 16.
options.C: True - because Railway Funds and Revenue are interchangeable under Demand 16.
options.D: False - because Only the General Manager's approval is needed to move funds between these segments.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation may be used to start a new service not provided for in the budget.

options.A: True - because New services are treated as reappropriation, not new expenditure.
options.B: False - because New services require a supplementary grant voted by Parliament.
options.C: True - because Parliamentary approval is not needed for new services.
options.D: False - because Savings can fund any new service the administration desires.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Railway administrations cannot sanction reappropriation after the 31st of March.

options.A: True - because Reappropriation may be sanctioned up to the 30th of June of the next year.
options.B: False - because The Board permits reappropriation until the accounts close in May.
options.C: True - because No reappropriation is permissible after the close of the financial year.
options.D: False - because Reappropriation after March needs only finance concurrence.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Under Demand 16, funds can be freely moved between Capital, Railway Funds and Revenue.

options.A: True - because Only Railway Funds are ring-fenced; Capital and Revenue are fungible.
options.B: False - because The three segments of Demand 16 form a common pool.
options.C: True - because Capital and Revenue are interchangeable for works.
options.D: False - because No reappropriation is permitted between these three segments under Demand 16.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation of provision requires a formal order.

options.A: True - because Transfer of provision from one sub-head to another is effected by a formal reappropriation order.
options.B: False - because Reappropriation can be done through an informal note on the file.
options.C: True - because Reappropriation is automatic once savings are identified.
options.D: False - because A verbal approval of the FA&CAO is sufficient for reappropriation.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Excess grants are based on the recommendation of the Railway Board.

options.A: True - because The Finance Ministry recommends excess grants.
options.B: False - because Excess grants are based on the recommendation of the Public Accounts Committee.
options.C: True - because The Board recommends excess grants to the President.
options.D: False - because Excess grants need no recommendation.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure on a new service not contemplated in the budget cannot be met by reappropriation.

options.A: True - because New services need only the Railway Board's administrative approval.
options.B: False - because The General Manager may start new services using reappropriated funds.
options.C: True - because New services require a supplementary grant voted by Parliament.
options.D: False - because Any new service can be funded by reappropriating savings.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation needs no formal order and can be done informally.

options.A: True - because An oral approval suffices for reappropriation.
options.B: False - because Reappropriation is effected automatically by the accounts office.
options.C: True - because Formal orders are needed only for charged heads.
options.D: False - because Every reappropriation requires a formal order transferring provision between sub-heads.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Savings should be withdrawn from disbursing officers as soon as they are known to be not required.

options.A: True - because Early surrender of savings allows their productive use for unavoidable expenditure elsewhere.
options.B: False - because Savings may be diverted to staff welfare without surrender.
options.C: True - because Savings should be retained by disbursing officers until March.
options.D: False - because Savings lapse automatically and need no withdrawal action.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Salaries of railway staff are charged expenditure.

options.A: True - because All salary expenditure is charged by the Constitution.
options.B: False - because Staff salaries are voted expenditure under the working expenses demands.
options.C: True - because Salaries are met from the Consolidated Fund without vote.
options.D: False - because Staff salaries are sanctioned by the President as charged.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Excess grants are presented on the recommendation of the Public Accounts Committee.

options.A: True - because Excess grants are recommended by the Railway Board.
options.B: False - because The General Manager recommends excess grants to Parliament.
options.C: True - because Excess grants follow the PAC's scrutiny of the Appropriation Accounts and the CAG's report.
options.D: False - because Excess grants need no recommendation from any committee.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Charged expenditure is voted by the Lok Sabha.

options.A: True - because The Lok Sabha votes charged demands like other demands.
options.B: False - because Both Houses vote on charged appropriations.
options.C: True - because Charged expenditure is approved by the Rajya Sabha.
options.D: False - because Charged expenditure is sanctioned by the President and is not voted upon.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Reappropriation should not be postponed to the end of the financial year.

options.A: True - because The position should be reviewed at intervals and reappropriations carried out promptly.
options.B: False - because Reappropriation should be done haphazardly as individual items exceed provision.
options.C: True - because Reappropriation is best done only in March when savings are certain.
options.D: False - because Monthly review of reappropriation is prohibited by the Finance Code.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The salary of the Chairman, Railway Board is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

options.A: True - because All Board members' salaries are charged expenditure.
options.B: False - because Only items such as the CAG's emoluments and court awards are charged; the Chairman's salary is voted under Demand 1.
options.C: True - because The Chairman's salary needs only the President's sanction.
options.D: False - because The Chairman's salary is declared charged by the Constitution.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
When additional funds are needed for new expenditure, a report must be submitted to the Railway Board.

options.A: True - because A report is needed only after the expenditure is incurred.
options.B: False - because The Board needs no report if the amount is below one crore rupees.
options.C: True - because The report shows the expenditure involved and the additional funds required.
options.D: False - because Additional funds can be drawn without informing the Board.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Appropriations for charged expenditure are sanctioned by Parliament.

options.A: True - because The Public Accounts Committee sanctions charged expenditure.
options.B: False - because Charged appropriations need no sanction at all.
options.C: True - because Parliament sanctions both voted and charged expenditure.
options.D: False - because Charged appropriations are sanctioned by the President.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The salary, allowances and pension of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

options.A: True - because The Constitution declares the CAG's emoluments as charged expenditure.
options.B: False - because The CAG's salary is charged to railway revenue.
options.C: True - because The CAG's emoluments are met from the Contingency Fund.
options.D: False - because The CAG's salary is voted by Parliament every year.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Dividend paid to General Revenues was a charged item of expenditure.

options.A: True - because Dividend was sanctioned by the President as charged.
options.B: False - because Dividend was a voted item provided under Demand 15.
options.C: True - because Dividend was met from the Contingency Fund.
options.D: False - because Dividend was not part of the railway budget.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Sums required to satisfy a court judgment or an arbitral award are charged expenditure.

options.A: True - because Arbitral awards are met from the Development Fund.
options.B: False - because Court judgments are charged to the Pension Fund.
options.C: True - because Judicial awards are declared charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
options.D: False - because Court awards are voted under Demand 12.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
A higher operating ratio indicates better financial performance.

options.A: True - because The ideal operating ratio is above 120.
options.B: False - because Higher ratios mean larger surpluses.
options.C: True - because The operating ratio rises with efficiency.
options.D: False - because A lower operating ratio indicates better financial health.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Appropriations for charged expenditure are sanctioned by the President.

options.A: True - because Charged expenditure is sanctioned by the President and is not voted by Parliament.
options.B: False - because Charged expenditure needs the sanction of the General Manager.
options.C: True - because Charged appropriations are sanctioned by the Lok Sabha.
options.D: False - because The Railway Minister sanctions charged expenditure.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The operating ratio includes capital expenditure in its numerator.

options.A: True - because Plan expenditure is part of working expenses.
options.B: False - because Only working expenses form the numerator of the operating ratio.
options.C: True - because Capital works are included in the operating ratio.
options.D: False - because The numerator covers all expenditure under Demand 16.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Charged expenditure can be discussed in Parliament but is not submitted to vote.

options.A: True - because Charged estimates are laid only before the Rajya Sabha.
options.B: False - because Charged expenditure cannot even be discussed in Parliament.
options.C: True - because Parliament may discuss charged estimates but cannot assent to, refuse or reduce them.
options.D: False - because Parliament votes on charged expenditure like any demand.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
An operating ratio of 100 means the railway is earning a profit.

options.A: True - because Profit is highest when the ratio is 100.
options.B: False - because A ratio of 100 indicates maximum profitability.
options.C: True - because A ratio of 100 means earnings are double the expenses.
options.D: False - because A ratio of 100 means working expenses equal gross earnings, leaving no surplus.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Pension and retirement benefits of railway employees are voted expenditure.

options.A: True - because Demand 13 is a grant voted by Parliament.
options.B: False - because Pension payments need only the President's sanction.
options.C: True - because Retirement benefits are met from the Contingency Fund.
options.D: False - because Railway pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Gross earnings exclude sundry other earnings.

options.A: True - because Sundry earnings form no part of railway earnings.
options.B: False - because Gross earnings include coaching, goods and sundry other earnings.
options.C: True - because Sundry earnings are appropriated to the DRF.
options.D: False - because Sundry earnings are credited to capital.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Expenditure of the Railway Board is voted expenditure.

options.A: True - because Demand 1 is sanctioned directly by the President.
options.B: False - because Railway Board expenses are met from the Consolidated Fund without vote.
options.C: True - because Demand 1 is a demand for grant voted by Parliament.
options.D: False - because The Railway Board's expenditure is charged by the Constitution.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The operating ratio uses net earnings in its denominator.

options.A: True - because The denominator is total capital-at-charge.
options.B: False - because Net surplus is the denominator of the operating ratio.
options.C: True - because The denominator is the number of staff.
options.D: False - because The denominator of the operating ratio is gross earnings.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
A supplementary grant is sought when a grant proves insufficient during the year.

options.A: True - because Supplementary grants meet anticipated expenditure in excess of the original grant.
options.B: False - because Supplementary grants need no Parliamentary approval.
options.C: True - because Supplementary grants regularise expenditure already incurred.
options.D: False - because Supplementary grants are sought after the year closes.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Development Fund is used for payment of staff salaries.

options.A: True - because Salaries are a proper charge on the DF.
options.B: False - because The DF is used for amenities, welfare and unremunerative works, not for salaries.
options.C: True - because The DF is the salary reserve of the railways.
options.D: False - because Staff allowances are paid from the DF.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Staff Benefit Fund is appropriated under Demand 14.

options.A: True - because The SBF is provided under Demand 16.
options.B: False - because The SBF is part of the appropriation to funds.
options.C: True - because The SBF is a charged appropriation.
options.D: False - because The Staff Benefit Fund is provided under Demand 11, Staff Welfare and Amenities.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Depreciation Reserve Fund is meant for payment of pensions.

options.A: True - because The DRF covers all retirement benefits.
options.B: False - because The DRF is for renewal and replacement of assets; pensions come from the Pension Fund.
options.C: True - because Pensions are paid from the DRF.
options.D: False - because The DRF and Pension Fund are the same.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Debt Service Fund is used for staff amenities.

options.A: True - because The DSF is a welfare fund.
options.B: False - because The DSF finances passenger amenities.
options.C: True - because Debt servicing is done from the Development Fund.
options.D: False - because The Debt Service Fund is used for servicing debt obligations.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Railway Safety Fund is financed only from general revenues.

options.A: True - because The safety surcharge goes to general revenues.
options.B: False - because It is also financed from the safety surcharge on passengers and other earmarked receipts.
options.C: True - because The Safety Fund has no earmarked receipts.
options.D: False - because Safety works are charged to revenue.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Appropriation to the Capital Fund is charged expenditure.

options.A: True - because Demand 14 is not voted.
options.B: False - because Fund appropriations are sanctioned by the President.
options.C: True - because The Capital Fund is a charged appropriation.
options.D: False - because Appropriations under Demand 14 are voted by Parliament.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Suspense heads are final heads of account.

options.A: True - because Suspense is the final booking for workshop costs.
options.B: False - because Suspense heads are transitory and must be cleared to final heads.
options.C: True - because Suspense balances are never transferred.
options.D: False - because Stores suspense is a final expenditure head.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) is a revenue suspense head.

options.A: True - because PH-73 is booked under revenue demands.
options.B: False - because Capital suspense does not exist in railway accounts.
options.C: True - because Miscellaneous Advances is Abstract N under Demand 12.
options.D: False - because Miscellaneous Advances under Plan Head 73 is a capital suspense head under Demand 16.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Stock under stores suspense represents stores already issued for consumption.

options.A: True - because Stock means stores issued to workshops.
options.B: False - because Stock represents the value of stores held in depots and stores.
options.C: True - because Stock is the same as purchases.
options.D: False - because Stock represents consumed stores.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Abstract N relates to appropriation to funds.

options.A: True - because Abstract M is suspense.
options.B: False - because Appropriation to funds has no abstract.
options.C: True - because Abstract N covers fund appropriations.
options.D: False - because Abstract N is Suspense; appropriation to funds is Abstract M.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Suspense balances are never adjusted to final heads of account.

options.A: True - because Suspense is written off to profit and loss.
options.B: False - because Suspense balances must be cleared and adjusted to final heads in due course.
options.C: True - because Suspense balances lapse like budget grants.
options.D: False - because Suspense balances are permanent assets.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Appropriation to railway funds under Demand 14 is voted expenditure.

options.A: True - because Fund appropriations need no Parliamentary approval.
options.B: False - because Demand 14 is met from the Contingency Fund.
options.C: True - because Demand 14 is a demand for grant voted by Parliament.
options.D: False - because Demand 14 appropriations are charged by the President.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Purchases under stores suspense record stores issued for consumption.

options.A: True - because Purchases represent sale of scrap.
options.B: False - because Purchases record stores consumed in workshops.
options.C: True - because Purchases are credited when stores are issued.
options.D: False - because Purchases record the value of stores received and taken on stock.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Debt Service Fund is used for servicing railway debt.

options.A: True - because It meets interest and repayment obligations on borrowings.
options.B: False - because The Debt Service Fund pays for passenger amenities.
options.C: True - because The Debt Service Fund is used for track renewals.
options.D: False - because The Debt Service Fund finances staff quarters.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Appropriation Accounts are audited by the Railway Board.

options.A: True - because The General Manager audits the Appropriation Accounts.
options.B: False - because The Appropriation Accounts are subject to statutory audit by the CAG.
options.C: True - because Appropriation Accounts need no audit.
options.D: False - because The Board is the final audit authority.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Stores Suspense under Plan Head 71 records purchases, sales and stock of stores.

options.A: True - because Stores suspense records staff salary advances.
options.B: False - because Stores suspense is a final head of account.
options.C: True - because These three elements make up stores suspense accounting.
options.D: False - because Stores suspense records only purchases of stores.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Demands for Grants are submitted for net expenditure after adjusting recoveries.

options.A: True - because Gross budgeting was abolished in 1979.
options.B: False - because Demands show net cash requirements only.
options.C: True - because Recoveries reduce the demand before voting.
options.D: False - because Demands are for gross expenditure; recoveries are shown as footnotes.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Workshop Manufacture Suspense records the cost of manufacture in railway workshops.

options.A: True - because It holds the cost of work-in-progress pending completion and adjustment.
options.B: False - because Manufacture suspense records purchase of raw materials only.
options.C: True - because Manufacture suspense records dividend payments.
options.D: False - because Manufacture suspense is charged permanently to revenue.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Allotments out of funds voted by Parliament are shown as 'Charged'.

options.A: True - because The voted/charged distinction was abolished.
options.B: False - because Voted allotments are shown as 'Voted'; only Presidential sanctions are 'Charged'.
options.C: True - because All allotments are shown as charged.
options.D: False - because Voted allotments are shown as charged in Budget Orders.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Suspense heads are transitory and must be cleared to final heads of account.

options.A: True - because Suspense heads need never be cleared.
options.B: False - because Suspense balances are carried forward permanently.
options.C: True - because Suspense balances are temporary and are adjusted in due course.
options.D: False - because Suspense balances lapse at the end of the year like grants.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The allocation code for revenue expenditure has ten digits.

options.A: True - because The code has ten digits including check digits.
options.B: False - because The code is purely alphabetical.
options.C: True - because The code has five digits.
options.D: False - because The allocation code consists of eight digits in three parts.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Demands Recoverable is a revenue suspense head for amounts recoverable from outside parties.

options.A: True - because It records claims recoverable from parties other than the railway.
options.B: False - because Demands Recoverable is a capital suspense head.
options.C: True - because Demands Recoverable records irrecoverable losses.
options.D: False - because Demands Recoverable is a final expenditure head.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Supplementary grants relate to expenditure already incurred.

options.A: True - because Excess grants are sought before expenditure.
options.B: False - because Expenditure already incurred in excess of the grant is regularised through excess grants.
options.C: True - because Supplementary grants are post-facto regularisations.
options.D: False - because Supplementary and excess grants are the same.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Manufacture Suspense is Plan Head 72.

options.A: True - because Manufacture suspense is Plan Head 73.
options.B: False - because Manufacture suspense is Plan Head 71.
options.C: True - because The plan head series assigns 72 to manufacture suspense.
options.D: False - because Manufacture suspense has no plan head number.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Cut motions can be moved against charged expenditure.

options.A: True - because Cut motions apply to all budget provisions.
options.B: False - because Charged expenditure is subject to cut motions.
options.C: True - because The Rajya Sabha moves cut motions on charged items.
options.D: False - because Cut motions apply only to voted demands for grants.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Appropriation Accounts compare actual expenditure with the grants voted and the appropriations sanctioned.

options.A: True - because They show actuals against the final grant or appropriation for each demand.
options.B: False - because The Appropriation Accounts compare earnings with expenditure.
options.C: True - because The Appropriation Accounts show only budget estimates.
options.D: False - because The Appropriation Accounts are prepared before the year begins.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Demands for grants can be presented without the President's recommendation.

options.A: True - because The President's recommendation is only a convention.
options.B: False - because Article 113(3) of the Constitution requires the President's recommendation.
options.C: True - because Demands are presented on the Speaker's recommendation.
options.D: False - because Only the Finance Minister's approval is needed.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts and the CAG's audit report thereon.

options.A: True - because The Railway Board finally approves the Appropriation Accounts.
options.B: False - because The Appropriation Accounts are examined by the Estimates Committee.
options.C: True - because The PAC scrutinises them on behalf of Parliament.
options.D: False - because No committee examines the Appropriation Accounts.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
The Comptroller and Auditor General is responsible for compiling railway accounts.

options.A: True - because The CAG compiles and audits the accounts.
options.B: False - because Compilation is done by the Finance Ministry.
options.C: True - because The PAC compiles railway accounts.
options.D: False - because The CAG audits the accounts; compilation is done by the railway accounts department.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Demands for Grants are presented for gross expenditure.

options.A: True - because The demands are for gross amounts; credits and recoveries are shown as footnotes.
options.B: False - because Demands show only the net cash requirement.
options.C: True - because Recoveries are deducted before presenting the demands.
options.D: False - because Demands are presented for net expenditure after recoveries.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Action on a draft para is required within four weeks.

options.A: True - because Draft paras need action within one week.
options.B: False - because Action on a draft para is required within eight weeks, vetted by Finance and approved by the GM.
options.C: True - because Draft paras are replied to within four weeks.
options.D: False - because Draft paras need no time-bound action.

q:
State whether the following statement is True or False:
Budget Orders are the orders by which allotments are communicated to railway administrations.

options.A: True - because Budget Orders sanction new works.
options.B: False - because Budget Orders are the same as reappropriation orders.
options.C: True - because Allotments out of voted grants and charged appropriations are conveyed through Budget Orders.
options.D: False - because Budget Orders are issued by the General Manager to Parliament.
